artists.biography:
Steven John Wilson (born 3 November 1967) is an English musician, best known as the founder, lead guitarist, singer and songwriter of progressive rock band Porcupine Tree. He is involved in many other bands and musical projects both as musician and producer (including No-Man and Blackfield) and also maintains a solo career.
Wilson is a self-taught producer, audio engineer, guitar and keyboard player, playing other instruments as and where required (including bass guitar, concert harp, hammered dulcimer and flute).
He used to split his living time between Tel Aviv and London, England, but he no longer holds a permanent residence in Tel Aviv.

perplexity.description:
Steven Wilson’s Cover Version, originally released in 2010, is a compilation album that gathers material from his limited-edition Cover Version singles series issued between 2003 and 2010. The album features 12 tracks, evenly split between six covers and six original compositions, showcasing Wilson’s eclectic musical tastes and his ability to reinterpret songs across genres including electronic, rock, folk, and world music. Notable covers include Alanis Morissette’s “Thank You,” ABBA’s “The Day Before You Came,” and The Cure’s “A Forest,” each transformed with Wilson’s atmospheric production and introspective arrangements. The original tracks, such as “Moment I Lost” and “Four Trees Down,” further highlight his songwriting range and stylistic versatility.

Released on the Kscope label, Cover Version stands as a unique entry in Wilson’s discography, bridging his solo work with his broader interests in reimagining and recontextualizing existing music. The album offers insight into Wilson’s evolution as an artist, reflecting his deep engagement with both contemporary and classic songwriting. While not a commercial blockbuster, Cover Version received positive critical attention for its thoughtful curation and the quality of its performances, solidifying its reputation as an essential listen for fans of Wilson’s genre-blending approach and his work in progressive and alternative music.
